result.title: Dynamics of Hidden Learning Structure
result.summary: A learner's present predictions do not fully determine how it will learn next. We study the dynamics of hidden learning structure through two related operations. Fiber Regulation Theory (FRT) describes protected repair of existing function and the learning responses left available after repair. Fiber Acquisition Theory (FAT) describes the formation and renewal of trainable structure, distinguishing neutral installation, access to a learning signal, and additional functional directions. The two operations also constrain one another. A repair obligation can force a change in a learning channel, while acquired features can make new protected repairs feasible or reduce the minimum coefficient cost of existing ones. We characterize joint admissibility and response reachability, and give a finite supervised-learning construction in which the two operations together produce a favorable response absent from either operation alone. We implement protected head repair and fixed-capacity LoRA renewal in Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, under replay and output distillation. Across two training trajectories differing in seed and within-task example order, the coordinated policy achieves higher teacher-forced Exact than either separate policy in all four comparisons. It also has the lowest macro NLL under both learning rules on the second trajectory. The implementations realize structure-conditioned self-regulation within specified information and action constraints: accessible state readouts and arrived evidence guide repairs and structural renewals, and ordinary learning continues from the modified state.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FRT 与 FAT 两套理论，刻画既有功能的受保护修复与可训练结构的新增更新及其相互约束，并在 Qwen2.5-32B 上用受保护 head 修复与固定容量 LoRA 更新做了监督学习验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 非视觉推理研究，但其「保留旧功能同时开辟新学习通道」的受保护修复加 LoRA 更新机制，可能为 LVR 中在不牺牲既有视觉表征的前提下扩充推理容量与监督分配提供线索，可供核查。
